Real-world capacity sanity check CPAP machines are unusually demanding loads for portable power stations — not because of power draw (most CPAPs use only 30-60W) but because of three specific requirements that knock out many otherwise-capable units. This guide explains those requirements, then ranks the seven best 2026 options for CPAP use. What CPAP machines need from a power station Not all power stations are CPAP-compatible. Three requirements: Pure sine wave AC output — modified sine wave produces audible buzzing in CPAP motors and accelerates wear. Almost all 2026 power stations are pure sine wave, but verify on the spec sheet. Stable voltage during humidifier kick-on — heated humidifiers cycle on and off, drawing 40-50W extra when heating. Inverters with weak voltage regulation cause CPAP firmware to log “voltage out of range” errors that wake you up. Long-life mode that works with low loads — many power stations enter “eco mode” below 10-20W draw and shut off the inverter completely. A CPAP without humidifier draws 30W, but during exhale it can momentarily drop to 5W. Bad eco-mode logic kills your sleep. What to look for before buying

Pure sine wave AC output: Verify that the model supports it, or use the CPAP manufacturer's compatible DC power solution.

Enough capacity: If you need two nights with a heated humidifier, consider a station around 2,000 Wh rather than 1,000 Wh.

12 V DC compatibility: A manufacturer-approved DC cable or converter can reduce conversion losses and extend runtime.

UPS switchover: Useful for home backup if you want power to transfer automatically during an outage. Confirm compatibility with your CPAP.

Low-load behavior: Check that the power station won't automatically shut off when your CPAP's power draw drops.

See the Mighty Generators CPAP guide and PowerStationTips compatibility guide for further details.

My final recommendation

For most users: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2.

For extended outages: Pecron E2400LFP, or an expandable EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus setup.

For travel without a heated humidifier: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus if portability and price matter most.

One question will help me narrow this down to the best choice for you: Do you run your CPAP's heated humidifier overnight? That makes a major difference in how much battery capacity you need.
